question.leadin: Answer the following about the rise of Rome.
question.text: Rome's first king and legendary founder was this man. This man murdered his twin brother, Remus.
question.clue: Fighting between factions loyal to him and factions loyal to Tatius eventually led to Numa Pompilius being crowned as this man's successor.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about Roman priesthoods.
swap.text: These Roman priestesses took thirty-year vows of chastity. The chief duty of these priestesses was to tend the eternal fire of Rome.
swap.clue: Livy claimed that a traitorous member of this group was crushed by the shields of the Sabines and then thrown from the namesake Tarpeian Rock.

question.leadin: Name these women who bedeviled the Roman Empire.
question.text: When this woman's husband Prasutagus died, Rome annexed his former kingdom, prompting this queen of the Iceni to lead a revolt in East Anglia that was put down by Paulinus.
question.clue: This person's popularity as a patriotic symbol in Victorian Britain was influenced by the theory that her name comes from a root meaning "victory" in Celtic.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Emperor Augustus's religious reforms.
swap.text: Suetonius (sweh-TOH-nee-uss) notes that Augustus revived this February festival, whose celebrants sacrifice goats, then don strips of the goatskin while running a circuit around the Palatine Hill that started and ended in a cave.
swap.clue: This event originated when King Amulius ordered two men to be thrown into the Tiber River as punishment.

question.leadin: The Creed of Ulfilas and Letter of Auxentius give us the clearest picture of this set of teachings.
question.text: Name this heresy briefly exonerated by the Council of Jerusalem which was named after a priest opposed by Athanasius.
question.clue: The emperor Constantius espoused this belief, leading to its further condemnation at the First Council of Constantinople.

swap.leadin: After being nominated to this position, one man defeated the Aquei at the Battle of Mount Algidus, disbanded his army, and returned to his farm in just 15 days.

question.leadin: Decabalus was the last independent leader of this region.
question.text: Name this region that was conquered by Trajan, which he depicted in his column. It had its capital at Sarmizegetusa.
question.clue: Soldiers of this region used the sickle-like falx during a war in which a bridge near the Iron Gates was built by Apollodorus.

swap.leadin: Answer some a group of peoples subjugated by the Romans.
swap.text: Livy describes how these people did not fare very well when Tullus Hostilius started a war with them. They are more famous for having their women raped by the original inhabitants of Rome.

question.leadin: The first secession of this group was on the Mons Sacer while the second took place on the Aventine Hill.
question.text: Name this most populous Roman societal class that forced discussion of their rights during the Conflict of the Orders against the Patricians by retreating from the city's public life.
question.clue: These people's legal status was ended by the Hortensian Law.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Roman Dacia.
swap.text: This artwork in Rome, later crowned with a statue of a saint rather than its builder, chronicles its namesake's conquest of Dacia.
swap.clue: This statue's base is composed of two blocks, and its top contains a statue of Peter.

question.leadin: Answer the following questions about the ritual of evocatio, in which a Roman general would "call forth" an enemy deity, offering it a cult at Rome and thereby depriving its city of divine protection.
question.text: The first recorded instance of evocatio was the transferal of Juno Regina from this city to the Aventine Hill. The supposed ten-year siege of this city, which fell in 396 B.C., is likely an artificial reference to the Trojan War.
question.clue: This city, home to the Grotta Campana tomb perhaps constructed by that king Tolumnius, was built around a sanctuary at Portonaccio with a life-size terracotta statue of Apollo attributed to Vulca.

swap.leadin: You are a sailor in the Roman navy.
swap.text: Because you are inexperienced at seaborne combat, you are grateful for the invention of this device, a large hinged bridge which is slammed down on opposing ships to turn sea battles into hand-to-hand combat.
swap.clue: This device that allowed soldiers to board enemy ships after a bridge with a spike on the bottom was lowered onto the enemy's hull.

question.leadin: A scholar of ancient Rome employed her expertise in this non-history-related profession to determine that classicists had been mistranslating the word "acus" ("AY-cuss").
question.text: Name this profession of Janet Stephens, who analyzed texts such as an epigram by Martial in which an enslaved woman with this profession named Plecusa is killed. Members of this profession used tools like vittae ("VIT-tee") and calamistra.
question.answerHtml: hairdressers [or hairstylists; or ornatrix; or ornatrices; prompt on stylists or salon workers or beauticians or people who cut hair; reject “barbers” or “maids” or “domestic workers”] {Acus is a catch-all term for several different tools, but in this context refers to a sewing needle used for weaving hair. Vittae are hair ribbons. Calamistra are curling irons.}

swap.text: Name this Roman historian, whose account venerates the military accomplishments of fellow pagan Julian the Apostate. His account ends abruptly as Fritigern and Saphrax are advancing their armies.
